reviewerOrPass: Worker B, separate same-AI source-first final pass, 31 October 2026
method: Worker B, separately identified same-AI source-first final pass. Reopened the current official 2026-entry common curriculum and all four dedicated major pages after publication, starting from the underlying requirements and academic questions rather than the repaired narrative. Reconsidered actual ISS/sustainability, brain/behaviour and legal/cultural subject matter, genuine choice and the neutral route hierarchy. Re-read actual current economic, organisational, sociological, environmental justice, governance, climate, meta-analysis, historical inquiry and child-rhetoric evidence to challenge the selections and alignments. Reconsidered the complete 54-course evidence and finished 72-placement/26-component record, interest roles and audience selections against those foundations. Same AI; not an independent person or human review.

academicFinding.external: Current main curriculum explicitly gives four majors and three themes. The dedicated ISS page establishes 24 EC in four first-year requirements, 18 EC of second-year requirements and two selected 6-EC major electives. With common core 36+12, theme 18 and final year 60, the coherent 26-component pathway totals 180 unique EC. Named required theme courses plus one further approved 6-EC elective reflect the published choice rather than a missing compulsory component. Five mobility choices remain genuine profiling. Theme capstone 12 and ISS thesis 12 are separate required projects. GROW 0 EC is separate. Dedicated ISS BSc statement controls generic BA headings; copied ISS headings on the other major pages do not conflate their distinct curricula. No essential unresolved formal rule remains.
academicFinding.neutralRoute: ISS is the least specialised social-science route spanning sociology, economics, business, law, philosophy and qualitative/quantitative methods. More focused brain, law/culture and design/technology routes were considered before selection. Themes have no advertised general/default preference, so official order selects Transformations to Sustainability. First two listed ISS electives, Statistics 2 and Sociological Themes, preserve general methods/disciplinary inquiry. None of these choices was based on UCR fit.
academicFinding.interests: All 68 rows reviewed: 21 generators, 33 support and 14 search-only. Eleven claims corrected with originals preserved: the omitted D&T major replaces a duplicate technology claim while row 10247 retains the actual Technology and Society theme; seven generic examples narrowed to verified question/elective/project scope or inferred applications; sustainability career specificity inferred; law/masters outcomes qualified. Human resilience/well-being has explicit CNB candidate ownership, supported by health, clinical, developmental and preventive psychology. Search-only examples/outcomes do not generate courses and are removed from constructive evidence; no residual catch-all.
academicFinding.closest: The final 24-course response materially studies the selected route: introductory, modern and contemporary sociology; qualitative research and statistical inference; economics, redistribution and welfare; organisational behaviour and inclusion; public institutions/law/ethics; environmental justice, sustainability governance, climate and sustainable communication. Seven substitutions implement these academic priorities instead of leaving major requirements abstract. Brain/behaviour and algorithmic/digital ethics retain interdisciplinary breadth. The spring inclusion course repairs a real fall-capacity problem while directly supporting people/community inquiry. This is a substantive programme-level response, not generic coherence or a limitation used to excuse a missing core.
academicFinding.CNB: The next concept materially answers the official brain/behaviour major through neural foundations, neurobiology, perception/action, higher functions and psycholinguistics, developmental/social/clinical/health psychology, experimental statistics and meta-analytic evidence synthesis. Sociological and philosophical inquiry, politics and AI ethics supply complementary perspectives. Clinical study does not promise professional qualification; meta-analysis does not become an independent thesis.
academicFinding.LPC: The third concept materially answers the actual law/political/cultural direction through public international, constitutional, rights, criminal, private and EU law, comparative/EU/international politics, peace/conflict, philosophical inquiry, rhetoric, history, media and literature. Gender, Indigenous and American-media histories provide real cultural/power substance without claiming European religious history. Description-only historical inquiry is fully considered on its stated research-question/source/paper scope; no archived Walcheren project or unsupported specific content is restored.
academicFinding.coherenceDistinctness: Closest, CNB then LPC each pass the sequential evidence, coherence, substantive distinctness and feasibility gates. Pairwise differences 14/18/20 courses (105/135/150 EC each) reflect genuinely different educational priorities, not renamed shared curricula. D&T is newly considered after three accepted options and explicitly stopped only at the maximum; no no-match or infeasibility judgment is manufactured.
academicFinding.implementation: All 54 selected courses and every actual contribution reconsidered. Each option has 24 unique courses/180 EC, four per term, Year-1 PPD and 7/9/7 advanced courses. All 72 offerings/formal prerequisites pass the sole current workbook. Foundational statistics precede experimental inference and evidence synthesis. Psycholinguistics uses its only covered spring offering after Brain & Behavior, with complementary Neurobiology concurrently; no extra hard rule invented. Read-only extraction pads omitted trailing blank fields, without changing the workbook or inventing offerings.
academicFinding.alignment: All 26 external and 54 UCR rows reconsidered. Seventeen partial substantive relationships retain the strongest adequate primary placements; nine gaps remain. Intro Sociology maps to the named major requirement; Social Psychology provides the defined individual/collective part. Python programming establishes algorithms; AI Ethics supplies human/digital normative interaction. Qualitative methods and two named statistics courses receive actual methods placements. Environmental justice and governance support the named theme courses. Ethical theory/free will/youth prevention are not forced into integrated Evil, Knowledge and Power or general Happiness. Neither child rhetoric nor group meta-analysis establishes the required theme capstone or independent thesis. Mobility, approved elective, Senior Seminar and other integrated gaps remain meaningful. Optional UCR research is additional unscheduled 15 EC, opposite required 12-EC thesis. Each UCR identity is used once.
academicFinding.disposition: Three repaired positive alternatives pass all academic gates. No unresolved source or downstream academic dependency remains.

The normal presentation distinguishes one comparator route from three UCR approaches, acknowledges required projects and genuine choice, and does not expose internal source/provenance distinctions.
